title: Plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene across dispersive and flat bands
authors: Antonio Palamara, Michele Pisarra, Antonello Sindona
abstract: The dynamical dielectric response of twisted bilayer graphene is explored in large-angle dispersive-band and small-angle quasi-flat-band regimes using time-dependent density-functional theory within the random-phase approximation. At the reference bilayer-graphene interlayer distance, weak coupling in the largest-angle structures preserves Dirac dispersions and the intrinsic $π$ plasmon. Electron doping activates a two-dimensional Dirac plasmon with energies obeying approximate geometric twist-angle scaling, while acoustic-like branches remain embedded in the single-particle continuum. The prohibitively large first-magic-angle supercell is represented by a tractable cell with its interlayer separation reduced to the angle-dependent magic distance, where four quasi-flat bands emerge around the Fermi level. Their partial occupation produces a dispersive low-energy plasmon-like excitation without a clear dielectric zero at resonance. A distinct interband plasmon is instead identified, supported by transitions involving the quasi-flat manifold and neighboring high-density-of-states regions. Band-energy rescaling places its characteristic energy in the mid-infrared range of interband collective excitations measured near the magic angle.
summary: This work investigates plasmonic excitations in twisted bilayer graphene by comparing its response in highly dispersive versus quasi-flat band regimes. Using TDDFT-RPA, the authors identify distinct plasmon modes—a 2D Dirac plasmon in the dispersive case and a mid-infrared interband plasmon in the flat-band case. This highlights how the electronic band structure dictates the nature of collective charge excitations in moiré materials.
main_problem: The study explores the dynamical dielectric response of twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) across different electronic band regimes, specifically comparing dispersive and quasi-flat band behavior.
main_result: In the dispersive regime, a 2D Dirac plasmon is activated by doping, while in the quasi-flat band regime, a distinct interband plasmon is identified with an energy in the mid-infrared range.
method: The research employs Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory (TDDFT) within the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) to calculate the energy-loss function.
model_or_system: The physical system is Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG), analyzed in three regimes: large-angle dispersive bands at a reference interlayer distance, and small-angle quasi-flat bands treated at a reduced, angle-dependent magic distance.
key_observables: Electron energy-loss function (ELOSS), plasmon dispersion ($\omega$ vs. $q$), and the dielectric function $\epsilon_M(q, \omega)$.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), interlayer distance ($d_0$ vs. $	ilde{d}$), and doping level (Fermi level shift).
main_assumptions: The study uses a tractable cell approximation for the magic-angle structure and is limited by the RPA approximation, excluding correlation-driven symmetry breaking.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of the three configurations, band structures showing Dirac cones and quasi-flat bands, and ELOSS spectra identifying the $\pi$-plasmon and the doping-activated 2D Dirac plasmon.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the dielectric response calculated for the dispersive band regime (large angles) versus the quasi-flat band regime (magic angle approximation), contrasting the resulting plasmonic excitations.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of collective excitations (plasmons) in systems exhibiting strong electronic correlations (flat bands) provides insights into how screening and charge dynamics are modified by proximity to correlated insulating states.
